modes.name: policy_claim_without_citation
modes.definition: Fail if the reply states a fact or rule that comes from a policy document but does not name that policy's valid identifier. Pass if every policy-derived statement in the reply carries its policy id, or the reply makes no policy claim.
modes.boundary: Nearest: policy_answer_wrong_or_incomplete. This mode is about a missing citation on a claim that may be correct; a wrong or incomplete policy answer belongs there, even when it is also uncited. Also distinct from the course demo mode unsupported_policy_claim (a claim the retrieved policy does not support). Batch 2: a follow-up turn that restates a policy-derived deadline (0035 T2, 0069 T3) needs its own citation even when an earlier turn cited the policy. 0101 and 0115 answered with no lookup at all. Batch 3: a policy fact relayed from a tool result ("5 to 10 business days" from issue_refund in 0072 and 0078) still needs its policy id, and so does a later turn that restates it with no new tool call (0058 T2, as in 0035 T2). Batch 4: naming a policy by its title ("the Saltbox Pantry store policy", 0123) is not a citation; citing an identifier that is not in the corpus (cw-orders, 0093) fails as if uncited. Close negatives (Part D): 0042 T1, 0051 T2, 0190 T1 make the same return-window claims and cite cw-returns; all marked no failure.
open_questions: Does RESP-1 apply to a refusal grounded in scope (SCOPE-2), as in 0125?
Citation presence is code-checkable; deciding which sentences are policy-derived needs a judge.
0101 is also incomplete (omits that a shipped order must be returned instead); first failure coded as the missing citation. Should it also count for policy_answer_wrong_or_incomplete?

modes.name: reply_omits_decision_basis
modes.definition: Fail if the reply reports a decision or outcome (a refusal, an escalation, an order status) but leaves out the reason or the material fact behind it that the tool results show: the closed return window, that the order is outside the caller's store, that the record is missing a date, or that a shipped order has not yet been delivered. Pass if the reply states the basis in terms the caller can act on, without revealing inaccessible data.
modes.boundary: In 0221 and 0183 the reason appeared only in the narration before a tool call, which the caller never sees; the system prompt requires that narration, so the reply must restate the reason. Nearest: inconsistent_record_not_escalated (0183 did escalate). 0076 is also uncited; its first failure is the missing explanation. Batch 3: 0211 (store's 7-day window not stated) and 0242 T2 (30-day rule not given) state an outcome without the rule; 0206 does not say today is the last eligible day. 0242 T2 also does not ask which item the customer meant. 0206 additionally never queued the $547 refund (ESC-1); see required_escalation_not_made. Close negatives (Part D): each states the decision with its reason: 0207 T1 (window closed, with the dates), 0047 T1 (shipped but not delivered, so the window has not started), 0079 T1 (refund queued because it is above the $100 threshold). 0175 (moved here 2026-11-09): support staff relayed a legal threat; the agent escalated (ticket 154) but only the narration said it cannot give legal advice. SPEC.md section 5 requires the reply to state both the refusal and the escalation.
modes.requirement_source: RESP-5 (explains the relevant decision); RESP-4 (explain refusals and escalations); RESP-3 (state missing or inconsistent information)

modes.name: required_action_not_taken
modes.definition: Fail if the turn ends without the write that policy requires and the agent had everything the action needs: an eligible refund at or below the threshold (issue_refund), or a case under ESC-1 to ESC-4 (escalate_to_human, or for ESC-1 the queued refund), whatever the caller's role. This covers offering or asking permission to act instead of acting, and deciding not to act. Pass if the agent takes the action in that turn, or asks only for information the action genuinely needs and the caller has not given.
modes.boundary: Close negatives 0072 and 0078: the caller stated the amount and the reason, and the agent issued the refund directly. 0243 never gave a reason and issue_refund requires one, so asking for the reason is allowed; asking to confirm the amount is not. In 0158 and 0163 the agent offered to escalate an account change every turn and never opened a ticket, against ESC-2 and the system prompt's "call escalate_to_human". Close negative 0252 T1: an account change escalated in the same turn with no confirmation step. Close negative 0248: the customer wanted "some money back" without an amount, so asking how much is information the action genuinely needs (the answer key expects it); the order total in the tool result is not the requested amount. Merged 2026-11-08 with required_escalation_not_made: deciding not to take a required escalation, as in 0206 (never queued its $547 refund for approval, ESC-1). Correction 2026-11-09: the merge was first argued from 0175, but 0175 did escalate (ticket 154); its failure is the reply leaving out the legal-advice refusal, so it moved to reply_omits_decision_basis. One product change fixes both: an instruction to call the required tool now, for any role, without asking permission, plus a guard that flags ESC cases with no escalate_to_human call. Nearest: reply_omits_decision_basis (the action happened but the reply does not explain it).
modes.requirement_source: ESC-1 to ESC-4; SPEC.md section 5 role clarification (2026-11-07); cw-refunds (refunds of $100 or less execute automatically once the order passes the eligibility check); system prompt escalation rule
open_questions: Spec tension: cw-account-security says account changes happen only through account settings, while ESC-2 and cw-escalations send them to a human. Record in review_summary.md.
The batch 2 role split (shoppers asked, merchants and support refunded) follows whether the message stated amount and reason, not the role itself.
0206 never queued the $547 refund (ESC-1), a later failure behind its first-coded one. Count it in Part E labels.

modes.name: reply_contradicts_tool_result
modes.definition: Fail if the reply asserts a fact about an order or product (that it exists or does not, which item or store it is, or a value such as a price, date, or eligibility) that the session's tool results contradict or cannot show. Pass if every such statement is supported by a tool result, or the reply states the tool's limitation instead (0089 T1). A value from the caller's message counts only after a tool confirms it (0077, 0249: the agent must verify any record fact it states).
modes.boundary: Nearest: inconsistent_record_not_escalated, where the record itself is damaged; here the record is fine and the agent misreads it. In 0013 and 0046 list_my_orders returned only ids, and the matching order was present. Close negative 0235 T1: the tool results lacked product names, and the agent asked which item rather than guessing; the answer key expects that. 0222 T2 is the weakest positive: the reply never states that no ticket exists, but offers to "assist in the escalation process" if the merchant confirms ownership, without mentioning ticket 159. AgentDebug would classify 0013 and 0046 as Reflection / outcome misinterpretation, but 0222 T2 as Memory / retrieval failure (the agent lost its own turn 1 ticket). If the search finds more cross-turn cases, consider a split. Search round 1 (2026-11-09): close negative 0089 T1 states the tool's limitation (no product or store names) instead of asserting absence. Rejected: 0145 and 0100 (the reply agrees with the tool), 0077 (the value came from the caller). Root cause (reviewer, 2026-11-09): most positives are presence, absence, or identity claims made from id-only rows (list_my_orders and find_order return product and store ids, not titles or names). The fix is for the agent to reach for another tool (find_order, get_order) or for the tools to return what the agent needs (titles, store names). Search round 2 (2026-11-09): 0249 is correct but unverifiable and fails (reviewer: "an agent that fails to verify is not acceptable"); 0077 joins as a positive under the reviewer's own note after its round 1 suggestion was rejected under the earlier definition. Close negative 0237: picked from id-only rows but every stated fact matches the rows.
